newsitem.title: FRANCE: French mountain rescue chief dies in Norway.
newsitem.headline: French mountain rescue chief dies in Norway.

text.p: The head of the French army's prestigious High Mountain Group (GMHM), has died from injuries suffered last week during a climbing accident, the army said on Tuesay.
Major Alain Esteve, 45, had been climbing a frozen waterfall near the Norwegian town of Hemsedal. He died on Monday in an Oslo hospital.
He never regained consciousness from head and chest wounds caused by last Wednesday's fall, an army spokesman said.
The GMHM takes part in Alpine rescues and tests mountaineering equipment and techniques near its Chamonix base in the French Alps. Esteve had been its commander since 1986.
He climbed Mount Everest without oxygen in 1993 and walked to the North Pole last year.
Esteve, who achieved the fastest-ever climb of Aconcagua, the Americas' highest mountain, also set a hang-gliding record and was a qualified helicopter and light aircraft pilot.
